root.label: Chronic Progressive Cutaneous Eruption with Hyperkeratotic Papules
supporting_facts: 10-year history of slowly progressive cutaneous eruption
presence of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the left leg
excluded_candidates: infectious etiology: no evidence of infection
malignant neoplasm: no history of cancer
other endocrine disorder: no history of other endocrine disorders
salient_findings: bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate in the superficial dermis

static_evidence_items.content: Chief complaint: 10-year history of slowly progressive, asymptomatic cutaneous eruption on left leg
No history of other endocrine disorder or malignant neoplasm
No family history of similar cutaneous findings
Location of cutaneous eruption: front and back of left leg from knee to ankle
Size of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules: 1 to 10 mm wide
Removal of scales caused slight bleeding
Rest of physical examination findings were unremarkable
Hematological and biochemical test results were unremarkable
Compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate in the superficial dermis found on lesional skin biopsy
